drafts.walkScript: Start with minute and hour. Sixty minutes make one hour, the next unit up. Twenty-four hours make one day, the next unit up again. A week is two steps up, and a clock is not a unit of time.
Start with captain and ship. A captain is in charge of a ship. A pilot is in charge of a plane, so plane fits. A wing is only part of a plane. An airport is where planes land, not what a pilot flies.
Start with bee and honey. A bee makes honey. A cow makes milk, so milk fits. Grass is what a cow eats, not what it makes. A farm is where a cow lives.
Start with sheep and lamb. A lamb is the baby of a sheep. A foal is the baby of a horse, so foal fits. A stable is where a horse lives, and hay is what it eats.
Start with spider and web. A spider builds a web to live in. A bird builds a nest to live in, so nest fits. An egg is laid in the nest, and a branch holds it up. Neither is the home a bird builds.
Start with foot and shoe. A shoe is worn on a foot. A hat is worn on a head, so hat fits. Hair grows on a head, so it is not worn. A neck is a body part below the head.
Start with kitten and cat. A kitten is a young cat. A puppy is a young dog, so dog fits. A bone is what a dog chews, and a kennel is where it sleeps. Neither is the grown animal.
Start with bird and nest. A bird lives in a nest. A bee lives in a hive, so hive fits. Honey is what bees make, and a sting is part of a bee. Neither is the home a bee lives in.
